title: arXiv physics weekly — 24–30 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart or readership statistics. This ordering is inferred from checkable current citation totals, independent topic or paper coverage where found, cross-listing, journal acceptance, data/code artifacts, and concrete results; citation evidence is sparse for papers only days old, and current totals are not period gains. It should be read as notable recent papers, not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: High significance measurement of reactor coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering on germanium by CONUS+
sections.abstract: The CONUS+ collaboration reports a 10.2σ reactor CEνNS measurement with high-purity germanium detectors and a weak-mixing-angle result consistent with the Standard Model.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 1,555 ± 152 CEνNS events from 1,296 kg·days of reactor-on exposure, 10.2σ significance, and sin²θW = 0.225 ± 0.022 at momentum transfer near 10 MeV, consistent with the Standard Model.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; blind likelihood analysis of CONUS+ high-purity germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the signal-count measurement remains statistics-dominated, while the comparison with the Standard Model and weak-mixing-angle determination are limited by signal-prediction systematics, especially energy calibration and the germanium quenching factor.

sections.title: Nongravitational Motion of 3I/ATLAS Far from the Sun: Robust Detection, Weak Constraints on the Activity Law
sections.abstract: Analysis of distant pre- and post-perihelion astrometry finds that nongravitational acceleration is detectable when the arcs are combined, but the data do not identify a unique heliocentric activity law.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find a clear nongravitational signal from combined distant astrometric arcs, with residual RMS falling from 0.33 to about 0.253–0.255 arcsec; water-ice and more volatile activity prescriptions nevertheless give statistically comparable fits.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; orbit determination and residual analysis of Minor Planet Center astrometry, with 8,498 observations available through April 2026.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report that separate pre- and post-perihelion solutions are not statistically robust, and residual non-normality and model-dependent outgassing prescriptions leave the physical origin and distance dependence uncertain.

sections.title: Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock
sections.abstract: High-power-laser experiments observe upstream emission and ion heating consistent with reflected-ion-related structure in a forming quasi-perpendicular collisionless shock.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report an upstream emission tail consistent with a shock foot and ion heating with temperature anisotropy upstream of the ramp, evidence for reflected-ion-related heating during early shock formation.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; high-power-laser shock formation studied with self-emission imaging and collective Thomson scattering.
sections.unique_caveat: The incident and reflected ion populations are not separately resolved, so the measurements do not yet directly establish how reflection mediates dissipation.

sections.title: Observation of measurement-induced localization phenomena in a solid-state spin system
sections.abstract: In an interacting ¹³C nuclear-spin system in diamond, more frequent single-spin projective or global weak measurements prolong spin autocorrelation, with simulations supporting a measurement-driven localized regime.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe longer spin autocorrelation times as measurement frequency rises and use numerical simulations to support measurement-induced localization in the diamond ¹³C spin system.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; nitrogen-vacancy-centre control and readout of interacting ¹³C nuclear spins, supplemented by numerical spin-dynamics simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: Localization is inferred from autocorrelation behavior together with simulations; the inferred spin configuration is non-unique, and direct measurement of the related entanglement phenomena remains future work.

sections.title: FastPM: Fast Pretrained Model for Cosmological Simulation-Based Inference
sections.abstract: The authors show that pretraining on inexpensive Fast Particle-Mesh simulations can cut the high-fidelity simulation burden for inference of Ωm and σ8, including tests using CAMELS hydrodynamical simulations.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed posterior accuracy, the pretrained model needs 5–15% as many high-fidelity simulations as training on CAMELS alone and can reduce total training compute by up to an order of magnitude; gains persist for the tested hydrodynamical matter power spectrum.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; transfer learning from FastPM simulations, fine-tuned and evaluated on CAMELS N-body and hydrodynamical simulation suites.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported gains are demonstrated for Ωm and σ8 inference from power spectra in the tested simulation suites; the FastPM pretraining itself contains no baryonic physics, so broader parameter and model-transfer performance remains unestablished.

sections.title: Ordered patches cap the stability of disordered frameworks
sections.abstract: The authors derive how ordered crystalline patches can cap disorder-induced stability gains in rigid-jointed frameworks under hydrostatic pressure, and test the criterion on Truchet frames and 876 slender-strut networks.
sections.claimed_result: The author finds that ordered patches under sufficient prestress localize failure once the local crystal instability threshold is crossed; across the studied networks, 798 of 876 fail first by a localizable instability.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; stability analysis of rigid-jointed frames, 2D Truchet structures, and a computational survey of 876 slender-strut nets.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is conditional on the rigid-joint, hydrostatic-pressure and prestress framework; it does not establish the same stability bound for real materials or other loading conditions.

sections.title: Environmental Quenching of Satellite Galaxies out to z~0.4 with GAMA and DEVILS
sections.abstract: A matched analysis of GAMA and DEVILS finds satellite star formation declining after inferred infall at about 0.14 dex/Gyr, with similar trends across the two surveys and no significant redshift evolution to z~0.4.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a steady post-infall decline relative to the star-forming main sequence of roughly 0.14 dex/Gyr, with consistent GAMA and DEVILS trends and no significant redshift evolution over the studied range.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; satellite samples from the GAMA and DEVILS galaxy surveys, with projected phase space used as an infall-time proxy.
sections.unique_caveat: Infall time is inferred rather than directly observed, and the result is limited to the surveys’ selections and redshift reach (about z=0.4); the analysis does not by itself identify a unique quenching mechanism.
